title: Homogeneous line bundles and regular semi-invariant sections
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Fix a split maximal torus $T$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, and let $Q=G/B$ and $\pi:G\to Q$ be the right $B$-torsor of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For any character $\chi:B\to\mathbf G_m$, the quotient of $G\times\mathbf A^1$ by the right action $$(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\chi(b)^{-1}z)$$ is a $G$-homogeneous line bundle on $Q$, whose sheaf of sections $\mathcal L_\chi$ is an invertible coherent $\mathcal O_Q$-module. Pullback to $G$ and the specified trivialization give an $F$-linear identification $$\Gamma(Q,\mathcal L_\chi)\simeq E(\chi):=\{f\in F[G]:f(gb)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(g)\text{ for every commutative }F\text{-algebra }A,\ g\in G(A),\ b\in B(A)\}.$$ The identification is equivariant for the natural left $G$-action, which on functions is $(s f)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$. An invertible sheaf means one locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Q$; coherent means locally finitely generated with finitely generated relations among any finite list of local generators.

source.place: Section 18c (pp.389--390), especially the quotient construction preceding Proposition 18.14; Definition 22.21 (p.468) and the proof of Theorem 22.48 (p.479).

proof.text: The cited Borel-pair result gives the faithfully flat map $\pi:G\to Q$ and $G\times_QG\simeq G\times_FB$. The scheme $G$ is affine of finite type over $F$, so its underlying space is Noetherian by lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components. By lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets, every open $\pi^{-1}(V)$, for $V\subset Q$ affine open, is quasi-compact. Cover it by affine opens and choose finitely many. Their images cover $V$ since $\pi$ is surjective, so the definition of fpqc covering applies. Thus $\{G\to Q\}$ is an fpqc covering, and remains so after any base change. We use the torsor isomorphism throughout, including over arbitrary test schemes.

source.place: Section 18c, p.390; fpqc verification using Stacks topologies.tex Tag 022B (definition-fpqc-covering), Tag 022D (lemma-fpqc), and topology.tex Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact).

proof.text: On $G\times_QG$, write the second point as $gb$ when the first is $g$. Give the trivial rank-one module $\mathcal O_G$ the descent isomorphism from its fibre at $g$ to its fibre at $gb$ given by $z\mapsto\chi(b)^{-1}z$. This is multiplication by a regular unit, hence is an isomorphism of modules. On the triple overlap $(g,gb,gbc)$ its composite multiplies by $\chi(c)^{-1}\chi(b)^{-1}=\chi(bc)^{-1}$; on the diagonal it is the identity. Apply lem-pc-fpqc-descent to this datum to obtain a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal L_\chi$ with $\pi^*\mathcal L_\chi\simeq\mathcal O_G$, including that specified descent isomorphism. The rank-one clause of that same node makes $\mathcal L_\chi$ invertible in the Zariski topology, not just locally trivial on the flat cover.

source.place: 18.11 and Section 18c, pp.389--390; Stacks descent.tex Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent) and Tag 05B2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-descends).

proof.text: Choose Zariski frames $e_i$ for $\mathcal L_\chi$ on $U_i\subset Q$. On $U_i\cap U_j$ write $e_j=u_{ij}e_i$ with $u_{ij}$ a regular unit. Glue $U_i\times\mathbf A^1$ by $(x,z)_j\mapsto(x,u_{ij}z)_i$ using lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes. The equations $u_{ik}=u_{ij}u_{jk}$ verify its cocycle hypothesis. This gives a line bundle $V\to Q$ whose sections are exactly those of $\mathcal L_\chi$: in these charts both are families $z_ie_i$ with $z_i=u_{ij}z_j$. The chosen pullback trivialization gives $V\times_QG\simeq G\times\mathbf A^1$. Its overlap map is precisely $(g,z)\mapsto(gb,\chi(b)^{-1}z)$ by the datum of step 2. Consequently $V$ represents the fpqc sheaf quotient by that right action: every $H\to V$ lifts to $G\times\mathbf A^1$ on the cover $H\times_QG\to H$, and two lifts with the same image differ by the unique $b$ supplied by $G\times_QG\simeq G\times B$, with exactly the indicated scalar change. Equality and gluing of these maps are detected on the cover by lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent. Since $Q$ is proper over $F$ and $\mathcal L_\chi$ invertible, lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent implies that $\mathcal L_\chi$ is coherent.

source.place: Section 18c, pp.389--390; Stacks schemes.tex Tags 01JB/01JC (lemma-glue, lemma-glue-schemes), descent.tex Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), coherent.tex Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian).

proof.text: First descend $(s,g)\mapsto\pi(sg)$ along the fpqc cover $G\times_FG\to G\times_FQ$: its values at $(s,g)$ and $(s,gb)$ agree, since $\pi(sgb)=\pi(sg)$. Representable descent supplies the base action morphism. For the total space, left multiplication sends $(g,z)$ to $(sg,z)$ and commutes with the right action, since $s(gb)=(sg)b$ and the scalar factor remains $\chi(b)^{-1}$. Use the pullback cover $G\times_F(G\times\mathbf A^1)\to G\times_FV$ and the map $(s,g,z)\mapsto[sg,z]$. It agrees on its overlap by the displayed identity, so representable descent supplies $G\times_FV\to V$ above the base action. Identity and composition follow by uniqueness after the analogous fpqc pullbacks, where they are $1g=g$ and $s(tg)=(st)g$. Fibrewise linearity is checked in the same trivialization, where $z$ is unchanged. Thus this is the required $G$-homogeneous structure.

source.place: Section 18c, p.390, sentence before Proposition 18.14; Stacks descent.tex Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: Pull a section of $\mathcal L_\chi$ back to $G$ and write it as $f$ in the specified trivialization. Here $\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)=F[G]$. The two pullbacks agree as sections of the descended module precisely when $f(gb)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(g)$. Conversely a regular function satisfying this equation gives compatible pullback sections on $G\times_QG$; lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent-fpqc-sections, applied with $S=T=Q$, $f=\mathrm{id}_Q$, the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal L_\chi$ and the cover $G\to Q$, gives a unique global section. The equation is an equality of regular functions on $G\times B$: its functor-of-points formulation on every commutative $F$-algebra is equivalent, as can be seen by evaluating at the universal point with algebra $F[G\times B]$. Thus the condition is exactly the stated definition of $E(\chi)$, not a condition merely on $F$-points. Both constructions preserve addition and $F$-scalars in the trivialization, and their composites are the identity by uniqueness of descent. This proves the asserted $F$-linear identification.

source.place: Theorem 22.48, proof, p.479; Definition 22.21, p.468; Stacks descent.tex Tag 03DT (lemma-sheaf-condition-holds).

proof.text: Under the action of step 4 a section transforms by $(s\sigma)(x)=s\sigma(s^{-1}x)$. Pulling back at $g$ gives $s[g',f(g')]=[g,f(s^{-1}g)]$ with $g'=s^{-1}g$, so its function is $(sf)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$. It satisfies $(sf)(gb)=\chi(b)^{-1}(sf)(g)$. This calculation also verifies the algebraic action, without invoking a cohomology base-change theorem: write $E(\chi)=\ker d$, where $d:F[G]\to F[G\times B]$ sends $f$ to $((g,b)\mapsto f(gb)-\chi(b)^{-1}f(g))$. For any $F$-algebra $A$, a vector-space complement to $\ker d$ shows $A\otimes_F\ker d=\ker(A\otimes_Fd)$. Hence the same descent comparison from step 5, applied after base change to $\operatorname{Spec}A$, identifies its sections with $A\otimes_FE(\chi)$. Apply the displayed action calculation for $s\in G(A)$, in particular for the universal $s$ over $A=F[G]$. It identifies the coaction on sections with the left regular coaction on $E(\chi)$, proving the claimed equivariance.
